paperTitle: Porting and Enhancing a Mental Health Narrative Game to Meta Quest 2 VR
centralContribution: This paper details the intricate process of porting and significantly enhancing a mental health narrative desktop game to the Meta Quest 2 VR platform, introducing novel features and optimizations to leverage VR's immersive capabilities. The work provides a comprehensive roadmap and valuable insights for future VR game design and development, focusing on performance, comfort, safety, interaction, and immersion to promote mental health awareness effectively.

content.description: Virtual Reality (VR), especially standalone devices like Meta Quest 2, offers immense potential for addressing global health challenges like depression. While games can foster mental health awareness, adapting existing desktop interactive narratives to VR presents significant challenges, including preventing motion sickness, designing intuitive 3D interactions, ensuring realistic embodiment, and overcoming hardware limitations. This paper addresses these complexities by detailing the porting and enhancement of a mental health narrative game to VR.

units.title: VR Controller Mappings
units.summary: Key VR headset and controller button mappings for in-game interactions.

content.caption: Meta Quest 2 Controller Mappings
content.description: Figure 2 illustrates the Meta Quest 2 VR headset and its controllers, detailing the button mappings (A/B for emergency pause/exit, C for movement/rotation, D for Oculus system, E for object interaction, F for grasping) used to enable 6 Degrees of Freedom (6DoF) interactions within the VR game.
Some screenshots from the perspective of Meta Quest 2 illustrate various virtual environments within the game.

Figure 3 shows various in-game text messages and dialogue boxes integrated into the 3D game space. This demonstrates the UI overhaul, where UI elements float and follow the player's head movement using linear interpolation for an immersive experience without distraction.

Figure 4 presents a series of screenshots showing the progression of an accelerated in-game day-night cycle, from 5 AM to 8 PM. This system simulates time, adjusting skybox illumination and contributing to the game's immersive environment.

Figure 5 visually represents or highlights the colliders applied to various interactable objects within the game scene. This demonstrates a fundamental technical aspect enabling physical interaction and collision detection in the VR environment, crucial for player engagement.

Figure 6 displays an in-game scene of a neatly made bed, symbolizing the game's core mechanic where positive habits (like making the bed) increase the protagonist's mental health level and reduce the antagonist's size. This visually represents the therapeutic gameplay loop directly linked to mental well-being.
Each consumable item in the sushi tray boosts the protagonist’s in-game mental health system.
In the VR game, players can interact with almost all objects, such as books, Star Wars figures, posters, and personal notes, by hitting and inspecting them.

Interaction between protagonist and antagonist via a standing mirror. The left side shows the external view, complete with an interaction button, while the right side offers the perspective from within the mirror.

Figure 10 depicts an in-game scene with blue arrows indicating navigation paths and a depression medicine bottle highlighted on the toilet floor, alongside an antagonist character. This illustrates the guidance system designed to direct players to interactive elements and target locations.
An example of a configurable joint object.

Figure 12 shows the protagonist interacting with a 'drawable object,' specifically writing 'SVR 2023' on a virtual canvas using an in-game brush tool. This highlights an innovative feature for player agency and creative expression within the VR environment.

Figure 13 displays an in-game wall painting generated using DALL-E generative AI from the prompt 'Blue and red butterflies feeling depressed, but still holding hope (Salvador Dalí style, on a light grey background)'. This showcases the integration of AI-generated art for dynamic environmental content.
